title: The late night shopping cart can wait until morning
dek: Things we add to an online cart in the middle of the night look different in daylight, and waiting a few hours can save money.
body: There is a particular kind of shopping that only happens very late at night. You cannot sleep, you start scrolling, and suddenly there is a cart full of things that seemed very important a few minutes ago.

Plenty of people know how this goes. A new set of storage bins, a kitchen gadget, a sweater in a color you never wear. When you are tired, a purchase can feel like a solution to something, and then feel unnecessary when the box arrives.

A simple rule can help. At night, you are allowed to add things to the cart, but you are not allowed to check out. In the morning, after coffee, look again. You may find you close the tab without buying anything more often than you expect.

This is especially helpful as the year heads toward the holiday season, when the ads get louder and the sales start earlier. A little distance between wanting something and buying it gives your budget a fair chance.
If you have a cart open right now, leave it there. Look at it again after breakfast and decide then.
